b01.note: Speed is rotation-only; 'up to' = equator. Draft said 'you're moving at' which ignores orbital motion.

b04.note: Sidereal 23.9345 h (NASA). Solar minus sidereal = 3 min 56 s -> 'about four minutes'; cause = orbital motion is correct.

b05.note: 2*pi*a/T_sid = 465.1 m/s = 1,674 km/h -> 'roughly 1,670'. 465 > 340 m/s so 'faster than sound' holds.

b06.note: Radius of the circle = N cos(lat), shrinks with latitude.

b07.note: WGS84 ellipsoid speeds at city latitudes; pole speed 0.

b08.note: Uniform circular motion at constant speed; centripetal accel 0.034 m/s^2 is imperceptible. Simplification acceptable.

b14.note: Newton's first law: unforced bodies keep their velocity.

b15.note: Relative speed to stopped ground = inertial speed, 465 m/s at equator, eastward.

b16.note: mu=0.7 rubber/dry concrete (Eng. ToolBox 0.6-0.85); a = mu g = 6.9 m/s^2; 1 s -> 7 m/s; 465-7=458.

b17.note: Draft implied open-ended tumble; scoped to 'in that one second' (<= 465 m).

b20.note: Energy-equivalent drop h = v^2/2g = 11.0 km > Everest 8.85 km; 'no air' caveat stated.

b22.note: Follows from rule one (rock and everything bolted to it stops).

b23.note: Draft used compression (bar) wave 5,000 m/s; a sideways base jolt travels up as a SHEAR wave, sqrt(G/rho) = 3,180 m/s.

b24.note: tau = rho c_s dv = 11.6 GPa (draft: 18 GPa from bar model).

b25.note: Compared against shear yield 250/sqrt(3) = 144 MPa -> ~80x (draft: 74x vs tensile yield). Conclusion phrased qualitatively.

b27.note: Air keeps eastward velocity; relative wind blows west->east at 465 m/s at equator.

b28.note: Draft said supersonic 'everywhere'. Only where v(lat) > 340 m/s: |lat| < 43 deg = sin(43 deg) = 68% of surface. Spherical approx, 'about'.

b29.note: q = 1/2 rho v^2 = 132 kPa is a LOWER bound; shock-corrected pitot overpressure is 196 kPa, hence 'at least'. 13.5 t-force/m^2 shown as 14.

b30.note: Draft showed 253 km/h (our own mph conversion); NOAA publishes 252 km/h - now uses published value. Ratio (465.1/70.2)^2 = 43.9.

b31.note: Draft said 'every obstacle on the planet'; restricted to the supersonic zone.

b32.note: 1/2 * 5.148e18 kg * 2/3 * v_eq^2 = 3.7e23 J (area-weighted cos^2 mean 2/3, uniform column mass assumed). / 620 EJ/yr = ~600 yr.

b33.note: 465 m < 500 m. ~95% of atmospheric mass lies above ~500 m altitude, so 'most of the air above the rooftops' is defensible; mountains excepted.

b34.note: Seafloor stops, water keeps velocity; NOAA mean depth 3,682 m.

b35.note: 465 m * 3,682 m = 1.71e6 m^3 per metre; /2,500 m^3 = 685 pools. Deep-water column assumption stated via 'in its path'.

b36.note: Joukowsky water-hammer relation dp = rho c dv for an instantaneous stop against a rigid boundary.

b37.note: 1025*1500*465.1 = 715 MPa ('around 720'); Challenger Deep 10,935 m -> ~110 MPa; ratio 6.5 -> 'more than 6'.

b38.note: Water moving east leaves west-side (east-facing) coasts; qualitative, scoped to 'near the shore'.

b39.note: sqrt(g*3682) = 190 m/s = 684 km/h, 76% of ~900 km/h jet cruise ('nearly'); NOAA itself says 'as fast as a jet plane'. 5,000 km / 190 m/s = 7.3 h.

b40.note: Honest uncertainty statement; no height claimed.

b41.note: Things not in contact with the ground keep moving with the air/orbit.

b42.note: At cruise altitude the air mass is undisturbed during the 1 s (no obstacles).

b43.note: NASA: ~17,500 mph = 28,000 km/h. Orbit is set by gravity and the ISS's own velocity, not Earth's spin.

b45.note: Anything that lost eastward speed is now slower than the restarted ground.

b46.note: Object at rest (inertial) vs ground at 465 m/s -> relative 465 m/s, opposite direction; 'up to'.

b48.note: Rotation phase permanently lags by 1 s under the scenario rules.

b49.note: 360 deg * 3600 / 86,164 s = 15.04 arcsec per second of time.

b50.note: Draft said Earth's spin 'wobbles' (wobble = polar motion, a different thing); now 'isn't perfectly steady'. 27 leap seconds 1972-2016 (IERS).

b51.note: IERS keeps |UT1-UTC| < 0.9 s, so a 1 s jump forces a leap second.

b54.note: Draft said 'every number was calculated on screen' - false for cited facts (e.g. ISS speed) and city speeds. Reworded.

b55.note: 'no surface' -> 'no solid surface' (NASA: Jupiter has no true solid surface).
